input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Spirit Airlines

output.company: Spirit Airlines (Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc., parent of Spirit Airlines, LLC; OTC: FLYYQ)

ownership.value: Publicly traded company (OTC: FLYYQ after NYSE American delisting Sept 2025). After its first Chapter 11 emergence on 2025-03-12, ownership passed to former lenders including funds managed by PIMCO, UBS Asset Management and Citadel Advisors. Since 2026-05-02 the company has ceased operations and is in a liquidating Chapter 11 controlled by its DIP lenders and creditors; equity holders are in line for residual value only.

financials.metric: Total operating revenues, FY2025 combined (Successor 2025-03-13 to 12-31 + Predecessor 2025-01-01 to 03-12)
Net loss, FY2025 combined (driven by $(2,832.7)M Successor-period loss)
Cash and cash equivalents (all of it: $273.0M of liquidity, unrestricted); revolver fully drawn Aug 21, 2025
Cash and cash equivalents (plus $396.1M restricted cash)
Liabilities subject to compromise (pre-petition debt incl. $275M drawn revolver, EETCs, PSP loans); plus $869.4M post-petition current + long-term debt and finance leases outside LSTC
Unrestricted cash, as reported to Moody's

debt_events.summary: Bankruptcy court (Judge Sean Lane, SDNY) approved Spirit's wind-down procedures (hearing 2026-05-05; order entered 2026-05-08): remaining aircraft leases rejected, owned aircraft to be sold; U.S. Trustee floated but did not press conversion to Chapter 7; Broward County asserted a lien on aircraft at Fort Lauderdale for postpetition admin claims

Having ceased operations on 2026-05-02, Spirit asked the bankruptcy court to approve an orderly wind-down/liquidation, saying it had 'no alternative'; sought $10.7M retention bonuses for remaining staff; liquidation expected complete in ~3 months

Spirit ceased all flight operations after talks over a $500M government rescue (up to 90% government equity) collapsed when creditors objected; ~$100M of incremental fuel costs since 2026-03-01 (Iran war) 'proved to be too much for its available liquidity to absorb'

Agreement in principle with creditors to emerge with debt and lease obligations cut from $7.4B to $2.1B, secured lenders to release cash collateral; emergence expected late spring/early summer 2026 — overtaken by the fuel-price shock and wind-down

Drew the full $100.0M Third Draw New Money Term Loans under the DIP facility (DIP Credit Agreement Amendment removed borrowing conditions; $50M of proceeds held in encumbered accounts; daily cash reports to DIP lenders required)
Court approved up to $1.2B DIP financing including $475M new money; DIP draws of $200M (2025-10-14) and $50M (2025-11-07); also drew the full $275M Exit RCF on 2025-08-21 before filing
Second Chapter 11 filing in under a year (SDNY, '2025 Bankruptcy') — 190 days after the first plan approval; triggered by AerCap default/termination notices; S&P cut Spirit to 'D' on 2025-09-02

AerCap (largest lessor) sent a Notice of Default, terminated the 36-aircraft A320neo/A321neo delivery deal and demanded $2.1M per aircraft (~$75.6M) termination fee; reportedly declared default on 37 leased aircraft

Fully drew the $275M Exit Revolving Credit Facility (due 2028); same month, amended credit-card processor deal requiring a $50M pledged account and daily holdbacks up to $3M until the bank is fully collateralized
Emerged from first Chapter 11: ~$795M of funded debt equitized plus $350M new equity investment; plan confirmed 2025-02-20, ownership passed to lenders (PIMCO, UBS Asset Management, Citadel Advisors)
First Chapter 11 filing (SDNY); Fitch downgraded Spirit to 'D' the same week (2024-11-20)

credit_ratings.summary: Fitch affirmed and withdrew Spirit Airlines' Long Term IDR (WD); placed Spirit EETCs on Rating Watch Negative — the final act after the wind-down began
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines' Long Term IDR to 'D' (default) from 'CCC-'
S&P lowered Spirit Airlines LLC's issuer credit rating to 'D' (default) from 'CCC'/Negative following the Aug 29, 2025 Chapter 11 filing; EETC issue ratings lowered one notch

Moody's downgraded Spirit's CFR to Caa3 from Caa1, PDR to Caa3-PD, SGL to SGL-4, outlook negative; forecast >$500M 2025 cash burn and a breach of the $450M minimum liquidity covenant as early as end-2025
Fitch downgraded Spirit Airlines to 'CCC-'; affirmed EETC ratings
S&P upgraded Spirit Airlines LLC to 'CCC+' from 'D', outlook stable, on emergence from bankruptcy (after 2024-11-18 'D' downgrade)

missing_fields: EBITDA / adjusted EBITDA for FY2025 — not disclosed as a figure in the pages retrieved (S&P projected ~7.5% adjusted EBITDA margin for 2025 in March 2025, but no actual figure was published)

Single total-debt figure as of 2025-12-31 — the FY2025 10-K reports debt within liabilities subject to compromise and instrument-level detail, but no consolidated total was extractable; nearest reported totals are $6,691.5M liabilities subject to compromise at 2025-09-30 (10-Q) and ~$2.4B long-term debt cited by AP at the second filing
Formal Chapter 7 conversion or final liquidation accounting after 2026-05-08 — no source covering June–November 2026 wind-down progress was available
output.risk_rationale: Risk is high — effectively realized. Spirit drew and defaulted on its obligations, filed its second Chapter 11 on 2025-08-29 after S&P cut it to 'D' (2025-09-02) and Fitch to 'D' (2025-09-04), and ceased all flight operations on 2026-05-02 after a proposed $500M government rescue collapsed; its CFO told the court there was 'no alternative to an orderly wind-down' and a ~$7.4B debt/lease load is being resolved only through bankruptcy (cut to ~$2.1B under the Feb 2026 deal before the wind-down). With FY2025 combined revenue down 22.7% to $3,796.7M, a $(768.7)M operating loss, cash of just $273.0M at 2025-12-31 and $6.69B of liabilities subject to compromise at 2025-09-30, any counterparty — ticket holders, vendors, lessors, employees — is an unsecured creditor of a company in liquidation; Fitch withdrew its ratings entirely on 2026-05-06. Do not extend unsecured credit; treat vouchers, credits and Free Spirit points as bankruptcy claims.

distress_signals.summary: Company shut down all operations; ~17,000 direct and indirect workers lost jobs; CEO Dave Davis: 'We just kind of ran out of runway'; leased planes returned, owned planes to be sold; not profitable since 2019
Could not fund an organized auction of aircraft/engines; asked court for fast sales or abandonment/repossession; headcount to drop from ~150 to ~40 within three months

Two senior executives (CHRO Linde Grindle, CIO Rocky Wiggins) departed; ~150 salaried corporate/operations roles eliminated; pulled out of 11 cities with more cuts (Milwaukee, Phoenix, Rochester NY, St. Louis, Bucaramanga) announced 2025-11-04
10-Q states 'management believes there is substantial doubt about the Company's ability to continue as a going concern'; operating as debtor-in-possession
NYSE American filed Form 25 to delist the stock; trading moved to OTC as 'FLYYQ' — equity effectively impaired in the second bankruptcy

Earlier August 2025 report stated 'substantial doubt' about staying in business; ~270 pilots furloughed and ~140 captains downgraded effective Oct/Nov 2025; ~$2.4B long-term debt and ~$1B negative free cash flow cited

payment_behaviour.summary: Broward County (Fort Lauderdale airport operator) asserted a lien on Spirit aircraft at the airport to secure postpetition administrative claims — an airport authority resorting to liens for unpaid obligations
CEO on the abrupt shutdown: vendors stop working and fuelers stop fuelling once shutdown looms — counterparties had already moved to prepayment/cash terms

AerCap issued a Notice of Default and demanded ~$75.6M in lease termination fees; credit-card companies demanded extra collateral as Spirit ran into payment difficulties and 'growing creditor mistrust'

Amended credit-card processor agreement forced a $50M transfer to a pledged account plus daily holdbacks up to $3M until the bank's exposure was fully collateralized — ticket revenue effectively escrowed
Solair Group, Inc. v. Spirit Airlines, Inc. (Miami-Dade Circuit Court, case 2025-005862-CA-01): creditor suit claiming interest on non-payment, restocking fees and finance charges
